sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The hooper is a Cornish folkloric figure. Writers also call it the hooter. It is a weather spirit, helpful but sometimes unkind. It resembles the Scottish Gray Man. The hooper is dense fog that blocks all sight. Or it is a cloudy curtain from a light shone in the center. Any person who saw the hooper stayed ashore, for a fierce storm always followed. One legend tells of a sailor who mocked the hooper and took out his crew anyway, against the warnings. His boat passed into the fog, then was never seen again.
objective: Document the hooper as a Cornish weather spirit
